Agentic ERP: Multi-Agent Architecture for Autonomous Planning

Abstract

Traditional enterprise software records transactions but still leaves difficult operational decisions to people.

This paper presents a role-aligned multi-agent architecture with a guarded planning loop and human approval for risky actions.

In a 365-day simulation, the agent system handled 639 orders and recorded zero stockouts, while a fixed-rule baseline recorded 302.

1 Introduction

The research gap is a system that combines flexible reasoning with auditable business controls.

2 Methodology

Five specialists use smaller tool sets and pass their work through plan, execute, reflect, and respond stages.

The enterprise state is represented as a tuple.

3 Results

The full system reached 100% task completion on 36 synthetic scenarios, while the single-agent version reached 83%.

The simulated system serviced 639 orders and the rules baseline serviced 300.

4 Discussion and Limitations

All evaluation data are synthetic and response quality is judged by another language model rather than calibrated human raters.

Generalisation is limited by the single small-business setting and the benchmark is not representative of production workloads.

5 Conclusion

Role-aligned agents appear promising when their actions remain inspectable and high-risk writes require human review.
